scale.description: Indicative transfer times and access facts for reaching and moving around Brittany from the family's origin airports (Lisbon and Porto). Times are typical scheduled durations, not door-to-door guarantees.

facts.label: Primary gateway: Nantes (NTE)
facts.value: Direct seasonal flights from Lisbon and Porto
facts.notes: Nantes is the primary gateway for all three route styles, with fast onward trains. Flight schedules are seasonal — re-check days before booking.

facts.label: Nature-route gateway: Brest (BES)
facts.value: Direct Transavia flight from Porto, Mon/Fri from 31 Mar 2026
facts.notes: Cuts the long transfer to the Côte de Granit Rose. No direct Lisbon–Brest flight for summer 2026.

facts.label: Train Nantes → Saint-Malo
facts.notes: Airport shuttle to Gare Sud ~25 min, then direct train. Schedules are seasonal — re-check before booking.

facts.label: Train Nantes → Vannes
facts.notes: The softest door-to-destination transfer on the trip; onward to Carnac by car or bus.

facts.label: Train Nantes → Quimper
facts.notes: Quimper also reachable from Paris in about 3 h 29 min.

facts.label: Train Brest → Lannion (Côte de Granit Rose)
facts.notes: Combines with the direct Porto–Brest flight for an efficient arrival onto the north coast.

facts.label: Rental car at Nantes airport
facts.value: Recommended; essential only where sights are dispersed
facts.notes: Public transport (trains, BreizhGo buses) connects cities and resorts but not beaches, megaliths, capes and island ferries. Saint-Malo old town is walkable; a car matters most for day trips.

facts.label: Driving own car from Portugal
facts.notes: Fuel and tolls ~€300–400 one way; needs a 2-day split with an overnight stop. Flying plus a local rental is the lighter option.
